findings.title: All success criteria trace to specific tasks
findings.description:
Cross-referencing the design's Success Criteria:
- **FR1** (no build path reads/writes `adoption.state`, runs detection, or spawns `sq`) → seam removal 3.3–3.6, code deletion 4.1/4.3/4.4, behavioral proof 5.1 (fake `sq` marker + snapshot), static check 6.2, manual walkthrough 6.3.
- **FR2** (brownfield Phase 0 → concept prompt, writes nothing regardless of state) → 5.1 runs the CLI path with no `.context-forge.toml` and with `in_progress`; 6.3 covers walkthrough steps 1–2 including the state left in place.
- **FR3** (byte identity) → 2.1–2.2 capture the two D6 cases on unmodified source, guarded at 3.7 and 6.1 with "golden files unchanged" success criteria.
- **FR4** (CLI/MCP parity) → 5.1 parity check, exactly as D5 describes.
- **FR5** (guide warning) → 3.5 keeps the stderr assertions; 6.1 names both existing test titles verbatim and forbids any changed warning `expect` line.
- **TR1** → 3.3 grep plus 6.2 repeat; **TR2** → 4.2's word-boundary grep plus the 6.2 export audit, which names exactly the design's three retained-module exceptions; **TR3** → full passes at 3.2a, 3.7, 6.1 (lint is the format gate, consistent with the Context Summary's "no format script").
- The Integration Requirement (269 starts clean) is enforced by the 6.2 export audit. Walkthrough steps 1–5 map to 6.3 plus 5.1/2.2/6.2. No criterion is left without a task, and no task lacks a criterion (branch setup 1.1 is mandated by AGENTS.md conventions).

findings.title: File-level claims in the tasks match the repository
findings.description: Verified against the working tree: `SectionBuilder.ts:161` renders the `Comprehension:` line and the two named test cases exist (`SectionBuilder.test.ts:167`, `:179`); `ContextTemplateEngine.ts:112-117` is section 3.4; `types/context.ts:39,41` holds both fields; `contracts.ts` contains exactly the symbols 4.2 removes plus the `ProbeOutcome` import (line 4); `adoptionState.ts:28` has `writeAdoptionState`; `adoptionOutcome.ts:15` has `adoption-completed`; `detection/index.ts:8-17` exports exactly the nine symbols 4.4 lists; `node.ts:60` has the comment 4.2 rewrites; `outOfTreeLinks.test.ts:13-16,88,111` uses `createAdoptionResolver`/`SquadronProbe` as 4.1 says; the two quoted guide-warning test titles exist verbatim (`build.test.ts:91`, `contextTools.test.ts:162`); the brownfield-guide fixture has `##### design` (line 23) and `##### Brownfield Adoption` (line 44), so 2.2's `design` instruction and 5.1's explicit-key assertion are grounded; `ContextIntegrator.ts:220,293` confirm the `dateProject` today-fallback 2.2 pins; `pipeline-integration.test.ts:129` has the `probeReturning` block 3.3 names; and `COMPREHENSION_PROFILE_VARIABLE = 'fileComprehension'` (`comprehensionAnalysis.ts:15`) makes 6.2's stated grep exception necessary and correct. Sequencing is sound: golden capture strictly precedes edits, 4.1 deletes `writeAdoptionState`'s consumers before 4.3 deletes it, and no circular dependencies exist. Every implementation step carries its test updates inline (test-with), and the two dedicated test tasks each map to a design decision (D6, D5) — no surplus test tasks.

findings.title: Commit markers are checkbox items and several tasks share one commit
findings.description: Commit lines are written as checklist items (`- [ ] Commit: \`...\``) rather than the plain `**Commit**:` marker form, so tooling scanning for the plain marker will not detect them. This is explained by AGENTS.md's "checklist format for all task files" rule, so no change is required. Placement is otherwise exemplary: nine commits spread across verified-working, tested points (2.3, 3.2a, 3.7, each of 4.1–4.4, 5.1, conditional 6.3) — never only at the end, never after every sub-task. The grouped commits (3.1–3.2 → 3.2a; 3.3–3.6 → 3.7) technically deviate from AGENTS.md's "commit at least once per task," but the file states the compile-coupling reason for each grouping, which serves the stronger semantic-commit principle.

findings.title: The typecheck-expectation note in section 3 is self-contradictory about `cli`
findings.description: The section intro says "Between 3.4 and 3.6, only `mcp-server` typecheck is expected to fail. `cli` passes once 3.5 is done." These two sentences conflict for the 3.4→3.5 stretch: after 3.4 changes the core signature and rebuilds `dist/`, `cli/src/commands/build.ts:84` still passes a second argument, so `cli` typecheck also fails until 3.5 — contradicting "only `mcp-server`." The intent (cli recovers at 3.5, mcp at 3.6) is recoverable and each task carries its own success criteria, so this cannot misroute work, but tightening the sentence to "after 3.4 both `cli` and `mcp-server` typecheck fail; `cli` passes once 3.5 is done, `mcp-server` once 3.6" would prevent a needless debugging detour by a junior implementer.
